newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
PRIME MINISTER MEETS PRAKASH HINDUJA

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram attended a private dinner with industrialist Prakash Hinduja, among others. The dinner rendezvous came even as the fate of the first set of Bofors papers sent to India on January 21, 1997 was unknown. The Hindujas were among the appellants in the multi-million dollar bribes in the Bofors case and were linked to the illegal payoffs. The Swiss Justice ministry identified three of the four Hinduja brothers - Gopichand, Srichand and Prakash - as appellants in the case. Secret bank documents linking them to the payoffs were slated to go to India with the final set of papers shortly.
The Pioneer
BOFORS FILES FOIL CONGRESS CHIEF'S GAMEPLAN

The recently acquired Bofors papers may derail Congress president Sitaram Kesri's plans to dislodge the United Front (UF) government. The documents may become a boon for the vulnerable coalition government by staving off immediate manipulation from Sonia Gandhi, widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi. Sonia was seen as the force behind Kesri's attempt for the Tamil Maanila Congress's merger with the parent party, without which the 13 party coalition cannot be dislodged. Congress sources said enough evidence had accumulated to drive home the possible impact of the Bofors papers. The papers were expected to throw light on the involvement of Italian businessman Ottavio Quattrochi whose
The Hindustan Times
FRESH POWER CRISIS LIKELY IN CAPITAL

If Delhi did not pay its electricity dues, its entire power supply would be cut off soon. A member of the Central Electricity Authority said the Delhi power utility (DESU) was unable to pay up the letter of credit (LC) amount worth 550 million rupees to the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC). NTPC, incharge of the maintenance and smooth running of power plants in the northern region electricity board, alleged DESU's LC amount was lesser than the number of units the latter drew from the power stations. NTPC had, therefore, started regulating power to the city. The situation was likely to worsen in the next few days.
The Economic Times
PRIME MINISTER OUTLINES FOREIGN INVESTORS' ROLE

The prime minister injected a degree of confidence among Indian business houses when he advised multinational companies (MNCs) not to use their financial clout to destroy or acquire small companies. The significance of the advice, coming within days of India putting into place a takeover code, was obvious. MNCs could play a significant part in helping the forging of partnerships, he said, and they should play a positive role by providing access to technology and capital. These observations as well as the finance minister's assertion that foreign investment played a role in the country's economic development only on the margins, appeared to be a new message defining the part the governmen
FOREIGN CHANNELS TO NEED APPROVAL

The government, through the broadcast law under examination by a cabinet subcommittee, has drawn up plans to regulate foreign satellite channels even if they were not uplinked from the country. The proposed guidelines stipulate that foreign satellite channels would not be received in the country unless licensed by the Indian broadcasting regulatory authority. The regulatory authority would be set up through the bill. This was the first time the government had shown its intentions to regulate the entry of foreign satellite channels into the country in a detailed way.
CENTRAL BANK SEEKS MORE POWERS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, would be amended to give the central bank greater control over financial institutions (FIs). Sources confirmed that a move was afoot to bring about changes, with the RBI financial institutions cell sending in recommendations to the apex bank's legal department for finalising the proposals. The RBI did not aim to have the kind of say it enjoyed on commercial banks but wanted greater monitoring power over FIs.
100 POWER PROJECTS MAY BE SCRAPPED

Some 100 odd liquid fuel power projects may be scrapped on account of the promoters' failure to bring in necessary foreign equity. They have also failed to sign the power purchase agreements within the agreed period. States had selected investors through tariff-based competitive bidding, before bidding parameters were arrived at by the union government. Respective state governments had directly cleared the proposals since every project had a cost of less than four billion rupees. Many firms had rushed in to bag the projects by quoting abnormally low power tariff in their price bids under the impression that there would no dearth of proposals from foreign power companies to sign joint ven
$525 MILLION LOAN FOR POWER PROJECT

National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) would raise a $525 million foreign currency loan, one of the largest by an Indian corporate. NHPC would be raising these funds for the 300 MW Chamera-II hydro project in Himachal Pradesh. The contract for the project was awarded to a consortium led by SNC Lavlin of Canada after a long bidding process. The mandate was likely to be awarded to Bank of America, ANZ Grindlays and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce. The Export Development Corporation of Canada would also be part of the financing package. The borrowing would carry a guarantee by the government and would be a long tenure investment for 10 years.
Financial Express
ADB CLEARS 715 MLN RUPEE EQUITY INVESTMENT

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) cleared a 715 million rupee equity investment in SBI Capital Markets to enable the company to restructure its operations. The move was in keeping with the Manila-based bank's commitment to pick up 13.84 percent stake in SBI Caps. Once a formal approval was accorded by the SBI Cap's board as also the central bank, ADB would be allotted 8033,707 equity shares at a premium of 79 rupees per 10 rupee share, sources said.
INFLATION DROPS TO 7.5 PCT

The pressure on price rise eased a little as the annual rate of inflation fell for the second week in succession to 7.48 percent in the week ended January 18, 1997. Annual inflation (provisional-over-final) fell by 0.16 percentage points compared to 7.64 percent during the previous week even as the wholesale prices index for all commodities (base 1981/82) registered a 0.2 percent increase to 320.4 as against 319.8 for the week before. Compared to this, the annual inflation during the corresponding week in 1996 was five percent.
MORGAN STANLEY TO FIND PARTNER FOR ESSAR OIL'S PROJECT

Morgan Stanley was assigned the task of finding a strategic partner for Essar Oil's refinery project in Gujarat. The investment banker was asked to have its recommendations ready in six months. The Ruias have a 57 percent stake in Essar Oil while financial institutions and public hold 10 percent and 33 percent each. The selected company would be offered 20 percent of the Ruias' stake. The nine million tonne, 54 billion rupee refinery was scheduled to go onstream in the first quarter of 1998. Sources believe the Ruias would consider multinationals as well as state owned firms. GOVERNMENT DIVIDED OVER DERESERVATION POLICY

Contradictory recommendations of two official committees set up to review the policy for the small-scale sector brought forth the differences in the government on the issue. The committee set up by the industry ministry called for total dereservation and welcomed investment by big companies in the sector. But, the commerce ministry panel recommended continuation of protection and reservation with minor modifications in the list of industries. The contradicting positions was likely to delay the announcement of the policy.
Business Standard
GOVERNMENT TO PICK MARUTI CHIEF

The government decided to nominate its own candidate to replace RC Bhargava, managing director of Maruti Udyog (MUL), adding a new dimension to the long drawn battle for control of the country's largest car maker. The industry minister informed Suzuki, which holds a 50 percent stake in MUL, that the government intended to exercise its right to appoint a successor to Bhargava, who was Suzuki's nominee. Under the existing agreement, the government and Suzuki Motors nominate persons to the posts of chairman and managing director by rotation. The move comes at a time, when the ministry, largely at the urging of the Prime Minister's Office, was against diluting government stake in the joint v
INDIA NEEDS $38 BLN IN TELECOMMUNICATION

The country will need an investment of at least $38 billion to meet the demand for telephone services by the turn of the century, well outside the government's financing capacity. This was revealed in the latest country study on India by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. The department of telecommunications estimated the total demand for telephone services by the end of the century at 40-50 million connections. The number of telephone connections in the country in March, 1996 stood at 11.98 million while the waiting list indicated an immediate unsatisfied demand of 2.27 million customers.
SETBACK FOR INFOTECH INDIA'S NEPAL VENTURE

Information Technology India Limited's (ITIL) bid to provide cellular, basic and international phone services in Nepal was held up after a local trade body challenged the decision to open telecommunication services to private operators. The Usha group company was among the three global consortia shortlisted for financial bids to provide services. The others were from Japan comprising Nippon Telegraph, KDD and Mitsubishi and a Swedish consortium led by Telia. ITIL was targetting the Nepal telecommunication services licence since another group company was holder of the cellular licences in Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar which share a common border with Nepal. DISCLOSURES ON ISSUE INTERMEDIARIES A MUST

The stock market regulator (SEBI) will make disclosures on the background of intermediaries associated with a public issue mandatory in the prospectus. The step was aimed at informing the investor about the intermediaries bringing an issue to the market and formed part of a series of measures being initiated to clean up the primary market. So far, SEBI had insisted on disclosures on either the issuer or the issue in the prospectus. Nothing was required to be mentioned about the string of intermediaries.
The Observer
DERIVATIVES REPORT ONLY BY APRIL

The derivatives committee, set up by the stock inmarket regulator to frame regulatory guidelines for trading in futures and options, would submit its report by April-end. The report, a detailed guideline for trading in derivatives, was expected to suggest various risk control measures and foolproof surveillance systems for the futures and options trading. The committee would also go into issues relating to threshold market capitalisation, volume of transactions in the cash market and automated settlement facility, with a view to evolving a detailed guideline for derivative trading, sources in the committee said.
Business Line
STATE FIRMS REJOIN FOR PARAXLENE PROJECT

Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) mended fences and once again proposed to join hands to implement the Hazira paraxylene project. The firms were considering a 60:40 joint venture with ONGC holding the higher stake to execute the 25 billion rupee project. However, the liquidity crisis prevailing in the oil industry has pushed the project into the slow lane. The patch-up notwithstanding, the project was unlikely to come up before the turn of the century. Although the proposal was submitted for first stage clearance, both companies, strapped for cash, are not keen to push through the project before the second half of 1997/98.
